newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish poll shows majority back revised EU pact.
newsitem.headline: Danish poll shows majority back revised EU pact.

text.p: The first Danish opinion poll conducted since EU leaders agreed to reform the European Union treaty shows that a modest majority would vote to ratify it if a referendum were held now.

The survey by the Greens polling unit, published on Friday in the business daily Borsen, showed that 28.7 percent would vote to accept the new treaty and 22.0 percent would reject it, with the remainder unsure how they would vote.
A political analyst said that the large "don't know" vote was unsurprising as the precise referendum questions are unknown.
Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen says that he will ask Danes to vote on the treaty changes early next year, but has set no date as yet.

Danes shocked fellow EU members when they flatly rejected the Maastricht treaty in 1992 and only voted to ratify it the following year on condition the Denmark stay out of economic and monetary union, a joint defence structure, cross-border policing and a common asylum policy.

The Greens poll, conducted on June 18 and 19, showed strong support for the admission of east and central European countries to the EU club, with 56.2 percent of the 815 respondents in favour of expansion and 31.2 percent against. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
